h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר ג׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Gimmel

p: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל נִקְרָא כֵּן
Shabbos HaGadol is called thus
דְּכָל הַמּוֹעֲדִים נִקְרָאִים בַּתּוֹרָה "שַׁבָּתוֹן מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ".
because all the festivals are called in the Torah "Shabbason, a holy convocation."
שַׁבָּתוֹן — שַׁבָּת קָטָן,
"Shabbason" means a minor Shabbos,
נ' הַקִּיטּוֹן, כְּמוֹ "אִישׁוֹן בַּת עָיִן"
with the diminutive suffix Nun, like "ishon bas ayin" (the pupil of the eye)
(תְּהִלִּים י"ז, ח'),
(Tehillim 17:8),
שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הָאִישׁ הַקָּטָן שֶׁנִּרְאֶה בָּעַיִן.
which is named after the "little man" (ishon) seen reflected in the eye.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
And regarding what they said in the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים קי"ח.):
(Pesachim 118a):
קָשִׁין מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם כִּפְלַיִם כְּיוֹלֵדָה,
"A person's sustenance is twice as hard as childbirth,"
דְּאִילּוּ בְּיוֹלֵדָה כְּתִיב "בְּעֶצֶב" וּבִמְזוֹנוֹת כְּתִיב "בְּעִצָּבוֹן"
for regarding a woman giving birth it is written "b'etzev" (in pain), whereas regarding sustenance it is written "b'itzavon"
אַף דִּלְפִי הָאָמוּר "עִצָּבוֹן" בְּנ' הַקִּיטּוֹן עֶצֶב קָטָן,
even though according to what was just said, "itzavon" with the diminutive Nun means a "minor pain,"
כְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁזֶּה הַמְכוּוָּן "כִּפְלַיִם כְּיוֹלֵדָה":
we have already explained that this is the very meaning of "twice as hard as childbirth":
שֶׁבְּיוֹלֵדָה הָעֶצֶב אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הָאִשָּׁה
for in childbirth, the pain does not come from the woman's own actions,
רַק שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַעֲצִיבָהּ;
rather Hashem, may He be blessed, inflicts the pain upon her;
וּבִמְזוֹנוֹת יֵשׁ כִּפְלַיִם:
whereas in sustenance there is a twofold pain:
עֶצֶב מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵהַקְּלָלָה,
first, pain from Hashem, may He be blessed, due to the curse,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן הָיָה אוֹכֵל מִפְּרִי הָעֵץ בְּלִי שׁוּם מְלָאכָה וִיגִיעָה,
for otherwise man would eat from the fruit of the tree without any labor or toil,
כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁתּוֹצִיא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּלוּסְקָאוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת
just as in the future when the Land of Israel will bring forth fine loaves, as they said in Shabbos
וְאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל כַּמָּה יְגִיעוֹת יָגַע אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן עַד שֶׁמָּצָא פַּת לֶאֱכוֹל
and after the sin, how many labors Adam HaRishon toiled until he found bread to eat
(בְּרָכוֹת נ"ח.)
(Berachos 58a)
זֶה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ;
this is from Hashem, may He be blessed;
וְעֶצֶב מִצַּד הָאָדָם שֶׁמַּטְרִיד עַצְמוֹ בִּמְלָאכָה בִּיגִיעַת נֶפֶשׁ,
and second, pain from man himself, who troubles himself with work in exhaustion of soul,
וְאִילּוּ הָיָה בּוֹטֵחַ בַּה' הָיָה דַּי לוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מְעוּטָה,
whereas if he trusted in Hashem, minimal effort would suffice for him,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא
along the lines of what is brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ס"ב:):
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 62b):
מַאי "שָׁטוּ" — שְׁטוּתָא הֲווֹ נָסְבוּ לְגַרְמַיְיהוּ וְכוּלֵּי
"What is 'shatu' (they roamed)? They took folly (shtusa) upon themselves, etc.;
מַאי אַטְרַח לוֹן כּוּלֵּי הַאי וְכוּלֵּי
what made them toil so much, etc.?
כְּגַוְונָא דָּא אִינּוּן דְּלָא מְהֵימְנֵי בֵּיהּ בְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
In the same way, those who do not have faith in the Holy One, blessed is He, etc.,
בָּעָאן לְאַטְרָחָא גַּרְמַיְיהוּ בָּתַר מְזוֹנָא יְמָמָא וְלֵילֵי וְכוּלֵּי.
seek to weary themselves pursuing sustenance day and night, etc."
וְזֶהוּ עִצָּבוֹן קָטָן מִצַּד הָאָדָם שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ לְהִנָּצֵל מִמֶּנּוּ,
And this is the "minor pain" from man's own side, which is within his power to be spared from
וְזֶה כִּפְלַיִם: מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִצַּד הָאָדָם
and thus it is twofold: from Hashem, may He be blessed, and from man
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא מַאֲמָר ו').
(and this was explained in Parshas Ki Sisa, Maamar 6).
וְכֵן שַׁבָּת נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן "שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן":
And similarly, Shabbos is also called "Shabbas Shabbason":
"שַׁבָּת" הוּא קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיְימָא מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,
"Shabbas" is the holiness fixed and enduring from Hashem, may He be blessed,
וְ"שַׁבָּתוֹן" — שַׁבָּת קָטָן מִצַּד הָאָדָם גַּם כֵּן,
and "Shabbason" is a minor Shabbos from man's side as well,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא תְּחִילָּה לְמִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ,
as it is called "the first of the holy convocations,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: זָכוֹר לְקַדְּשׁוֹ, שָׁמוֹר לְקַדְּשׁוֹ.
as it is said: "Remember [the Shabbos day] to sanctify it," "Observe [the Shabbos day] to sanctify it."
וְיוֹם טוֹב נִקְרָא רַק "שַׁבָּתוֹן", שַׁבָּת קָטָן מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
Whereas a Festival is called only "Shabbason," a minor Shabbos from Israel's side,
דִּמְעַבְּרִי לְיַרְחָא וְקָבְעִי לִשְׁנֵי,
because Israel intercalate the months and establish the years,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים
as they said in Pesachim
וּבְפֶסַח לֹא כְּתִיב שַׁבָּתוֹן רַק מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ, וְכֵן בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת.
And regarding Pesach, "Shabbason" is not written, only "holy convocation," and likewise regarding Shavuos.
וְהַטַּעַם: דְּפֶסַח נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת,
And the reason is that Pesach is called "Shabbos,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(וַיִּקְרָא כ"ג, ט"ו):
(Vayikra 23:15):
וּסְפַרְתֶּם לָכֶם מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת וְגוֹמֵר,
"And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ דִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַפֶּסַח הָיָה בְּלֹא הֲכָנָה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
That is, the holiness of Pesach came without preparation from Israel's side,
רַק מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּחַסְדּוֹ,
solely from Hashem, may He be blessed, in His kindness,
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת.
and therefore it is called "Shabbos."
וְכֵן שָׁבוּעוֹת זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְהַתְחָלַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And likewise Shavuos, the time of the Giving of the Torah, was the initiation of holiness from Hashem, may He be blessed
וְזֶה הָיָה בִּשְׁנַת יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
and this was in the year of the Exodus from Egypt.
אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁאֵין יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וְאֵין מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
However, afterward, when there is no actual Exodus from Egypt and no Giving of the Torah,
תּוּ לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לִקְרוֹתוֹ לֹא שַׁבָּת
it is no longer applicable to call it "Shabbos,"
כֵּיוָן דְּהַקְּדוּשָּׁה הָיָה רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה,
since that holiness was only temporary,
וְלֹא שַׁבָּתוֹן
nor "Shabbason,"
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה אֵינָהּ מִצַּד הָאָדָם.
since the holiness does not originate from man.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְסוּכּוֹת נִקְרָאִים בְּפָרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר "שַׁבָּתוֹן",
Not so Rosh Hashanah and Sukkos, which are called "Shabbason" in Parshas Emor
מִצַּד הָאָדָם, שַׁבָּת קָטָן כָּאָמוּר.
from man's side, a minor Shabbos, as stated.
וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים "שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן":
And Yom Kippur is called "Shabbas Shabbason":
"שַׁבָּת" — קְדוּשָּׁה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, יוֹם שֶׁנִּיתְּנוּ בּוֹ לוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת,
"Shabbas"—holiness from Hashem, may He be blessed, the day on which the second Tablets were given;
וְ"שַׁבָּתוֹן" — מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and "Shabbason"—a holy convocation from Israel's side.
וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ אַף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִמַּתַּן לוּחוֹת,
And so too afterward, even though it no longer has the holiness from Hashem, may He be blessed, of the giving of the Tablets,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן שַׁבָּת
nevertheless it is still called "Shabbos,"
שֶׁהוּא יוֹם סְלִיחָה וּמְחִילָה לְדוֹרוֹת,
because it is a day of pardon and forgiveness for all generations,
וְהוּא שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, בִּינָה, עָלְמָא דְּחֵירוּ, עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי,
and it is Shabbos HaGadol, Binah, the World of Freedom, the World to Come
וְ"שַׁבָּתוֹן" מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and "Shabbason" from Israel's side.
וּבְפֶסַח לֹא נִזְכַּר שַׁבָּת בְּפָרָשַׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים רַק בִּסְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר,
And regarding Pesach, "Shabbos" is not mentioned in the section of the festivals except in connection with Sefiras HaOmer,
שֶׁהַסְּפִירָה מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבוּעָא וְקַיְימָא מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,
because the counting comes from the holiness that is fixed and enduring from Hashem, may He be blessed,
וְזֶהוּ שַׁבָּת.
and that is Shabbos.
וְעַל זֶה נִצְטַוִּינוּ לִסְפּוֹר שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע
And regarding this we were commanded to count seven times seven,
לִזְכּוֹת לְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה אַחַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת.
to merit that holiness after being refined sevenfold to be purified in all the attributes.
וְשַׁבָּת כּוֹלֵל כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים שֶׁאַחֲרָיו בְּשִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
And Shabbos encompasses all the holiness of the festivals that follow it during the seven weekdays,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: בֵּרַכְתּוֹ מִכָּל הַיָּמִים קִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים,
as we say: "You blessed it above all days, You sanctified it above all seasons,"
שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה
for it is the source of blessing
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' פ"ח.).
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 88a).
לָכֵן שַׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם הַפֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרְגָלִים
Therefore, the Shabbos before Pesach—which is the New Year for the pilgrimage festivals
כּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַּׁת הֶחָג שֶׁאַחֲרָיו בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּתוֹן, שַׁבָּת קָטָן,
encompasses the holiness of the festival following it in the weekdays, which is "Shabbason," a minor Shabbos,
וְהוּא, שַׁבָּת הַקּוֹדֵם לוֹ, נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל כָּאָמוּר.
and it—the Shabbos preceding it—is called Shabbos HaGadol, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 58a — Ben Zoma "used to say: How many labors Adam HaRishon toiled until he found bread to eat! He plowed, sowed, reaped, bound sheaves, threshed, winnowed, selected, ground, sifted, kneaded and baked, and only then ate. And I rise and find all these prepared before me." Rashi (on "all nations come to my door"): he was wealthy, and everyone came to him to trade.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 62b (Beshalach) — "What is 'shatu' (they roamed, Bamidbar 11:8)? They took folly (shtusa) upon themselves, because they were not people of faith... Who made them toil so much? Only that they were not people of faith. So too those who do not believe in the Holy One, blessed is He, and do not wish to look into His ways: they weary themselves every day after sustenance, day and night, lest they not obtain a piece of bread."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rabbeinu Bachya, Devarim 32:10 — “‘As the pupil (ishon) of His eye’: the pupil of the eye is called ishon because the form of a man (ish) appears in it, and the form ishon refers to the smallness of the form. So too, ‘Shabbas Shabbason’: ‘Shabbas’ is said of the essence of the day, and ‘Shabbason’ is said of the addition, and it is a diminutive form. And so too the form Aminon for Amnon.” Connection: Rav Tzadok and Rabbeinu Bachya both read the final Nun of ‘Shabbason’ as a diminutive like ishon and distinguish it from ‘Shabbas,’ the essence of the day; Rabbeinu Bachya identifies the lesser ‘Shabbason’ as the added time, the part that man adds to the holy day himself, which fits Rav Tzadok's ‘minor Shabbos from man's side.’

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shabbos HaGadol 5 — “The holiness of Shabbos is fixed and established from His side, so that there is no room in it for human action. Therefore even preparing food is forbidden on it. But the holiness of the festivals is that Israel sanctify them through their service: they draw this holiness from Shabbos to themselves through service within their grasp. Therefore preparing food is permitted then, to show that there is room in it for human grasp. And from where does a person get the power to sanctify the times? It spreads from the holiness of Shabbos.” Connection: Both set Shabbos, holy from Hashem, against Yom Tov, made holy by Israel and drawing from Shabbos; Sod Yesharim shows the distinction in the permission to prepare food on Yom Tov.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Pesach 5647 — “The difference between Shabbos and the festivals: Shabbos is a gift, as it says, ‘I have a good gift in My treasure house … go and inform them’; but the festivals Israel merit through their own selves, as it says, ‘Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons,’ and ‘holy convocations which you shall call.’ Therefore there is rejoicing on the festivals, for one who eats what is not his own is ashamed to look up. Through the festivals the knowledge of Shabbos's light spreads out. The holiness renewed on the festivals would not be revealed below were it not for the preparation made in Israel, who are vessels to receive these lights; therefore it says ‘which you shall call’: Israel sanctify the seasons.” Connection: Both set the fixed holiness of Shabbos, given from Above, against the festivals' holiness, which comes from Israel's side; Sefas Emes adds that this is why festivals carry a joy of one's own earning, and that through them the hidden light of Shabbos spreads out.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 117b — "Shabbos is fixed and established [of itself], so both in prayer and in Kiddush we say 'Who sanctifies the Shabbos.' Yom Tov, it is Israel who fix it, for they intercalate the months and fix the years; therefore we say 'Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.'" Rashbam: Shabbos is fixed "from the six days of Creation, and does not depend on the fixing of the new month."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 88a (Yisro) — "All the blessings above and below depend on the seventh day. And why was no manna found on the seventh day? Because from that day all six supernal days are blessed, and each one gives its sustenance below, each on its own day, from that blessing with which they are blessed on the seventh day."
